extracted.intended_audience: leaders, staff, and administrators of cultural organizations, artist collectives, archives, and researchers seeking Mellon Foundation Arts & Culture funding
extracted.subtask_short: applying to mellon arts & culture grants
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Mellon Foundation’s Arts & Culture grant priorities and how their grantmaking operates; useful for organizations, archives, collectives, and researchers considering or preparing for Mellon support. Emphasizes types of recipients supported and the invitation-based outreach model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for cultural organizations demonstrating visionary leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural organizations that are driving models of visionary leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mellon prioritizes cultural organizations that exemplify or advance new/visionary leadership models. Applicants should demonstrate organizational leadership, strategic vision, or model-building capacity that could influence or inspire the broader field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for institutions, collectives, and initiatives creating new forms of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions, collectives, and initiatives that are creating new forms of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is intended for entities engaged in artistic innovation and experimentation—those developing new forms, practices, or modes of cultural expression. Proposals should clearly show how the work expands or transforms artistic practice or audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for artistic archives focused on preservation and restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Artistic archives that preserve or restore important work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mellon funds archives whose preservation or restoration work safeguards culturally or artistically significant materials. Emphasize archival significance, preservation methodology, access/outreach plans, and the ways restoration/preservation sustains artistic legacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for research that strengthens the creative sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that can help us understand and create a more viable creative sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research projects should generate knowledge or tools that improve the health, sustainability, or equity of the creative sector. Proposals should show clear relevance to sector viability and potential for practical impact on institutions, policy, or practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: grants to eligible recipients aligned with Mellon priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Through grants to eligible recipients, we support: Cultural organizations; Institutions, collectives, and initiatives; Artistic archives; Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is tied to the categories above and alignment with Mellon’s Arts & Culture priorities. Applicants should verify they fit one of the supported recipient types and that their work aligns with the foundation’s stated focus areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation-based grantmaking and staff outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Our staff seek out and get to know innovative organizations, scholars, and creators before inviting them to submit a proposal for funding. Most Mellon grants are made through these invitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mellon’s process is largely proactive: staff identify and cultivate relationships with potential grantees and extend invitations to apply. Organizations should anticipate that unsolicited applications may be less common and that relationship-building with program staff can be an important precursor to funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantmaking purpose: catalytic support for expression and ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Our grantmaking is a catalyst for expression and ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants are intended to catalyze artistic expression, new ideas, and sector innovation rather than merely maintain existing operations. Applicants should articulate how funding would enable transformative projects, new thinking, or significant expansion of impact.
